record.original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R be a finitely generated factorial K-domain, let L=Q(R), and let δ be a K-derivation of R. If X_δ denotes the monoid of δ-integral factors in R and tilde_X_δ denotes the abelian group of δ-integral factors in L, is tilde_X_δ necessarily a finitely generated abelian group?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 1. With the notations and assumptions as above, is ˜Xδ a ﬁnitely generated abelian group provided R is ﬁnitely generated over K ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $R$ be a finitely generated factorial (i.e., unique factorization) $K$-domain. Let $L = Q(R)$ denote the field of fractions of $R$, and let $\delta\colon R \to R$ be a $K$-derivation, extended uniquely to a $K$-derivation of $L$, still denoted $\delta$.

A nonzero element $f \in R$ is called a $\delta$-integral factor (in $R$) if there exists $g \in R$ with $\delta(f) = g f$; equivalently, the logarithmic derivative $\delta(f)/f$ lies in $R$. A nonzero element $h \in L$ is called a $\delta$-integral factor in $L$ if $\delta(h)/h \in R$. The set $X_\delta$ of $\delta$-integral factors in $R$, taken modulo units of $R$, forms a commutative monoid under multiplication, and the set $\widetilde{X}_\delta$ of $\delta$-integral factors in $L$, taken modulo units of $R$, forms an abelian group under multiplication (its elements being represented by quotients $f_1/f_2$ of $\delta$-integral factors $f_1, f_2 \in R$).

Question: Must $\widetilde{X}_\delta$ be a finitely generated abelian group?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not locate a definitive resolution of this question concerning finite generation of the group of δ-integral factors (closely related to Darboux polynomials/logarithmic derivatives) for arbitrary K-derivations of finitely generated factorial K-domains. The problem appears to remain open in this generality, but no authoritative confirmation of its current status was found.

status_evidence.title: Constructing (Almost) Rigid Rings and a UFD Having Infinitely Generated Derksen and Makar-Limanov Invariants
status_evidence.snippet: UFDs and associated invariants of derivations, some of which can fail to be finitely generated
status_evidence.claim: Related invariants of derivations on UFDs are studied and can in some cases be infinitely generated, indicating subtle finiteness behavior.

status_evidence.title: Computation of Darboux polynomials and rational first integrals
status_evidence.snippet: Darboux polynomials are nonzero polynomials f with delta(f) = g f for some polynomial g.
status_evidence.claim: The δ-integral factors in R coincide with Darboux polynomials of δ, a well-studied object.
